reason: E2 supports grain refinement strengthening in a different alloy system (TRIP-HEA) but not in MnNiSi-based materials. E1 shows that nanocrystalline samples have lower maximum entropy change than bulk, supporting the premise that excessive grain refinement can degrade magnetocaloric performance, but provides no evidence that moderate grain refinement preserves the magnetocaloric effect or that TMP can achieve such refinement in these materials. The core premises about TMP applicability and the existence of an optimal grain size window in MnNiSi are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Grain refinement enhances mechanical strength via the Hall–Petch effect
The magneto-structural transition responsible for the magnetocaloric effect remains largely unaltered if grain size is within an optimal window
Thermomechanical processing (cold-rolling + annealing) can refine grain structure in MnNiSi-based compounds
Nanocrystalline grain sizes can reduce magnetic entropy change compared to bulk
